To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a new approach to behavioral synthesis that considers memory mapping and memory architecture.

1) the memory mapping can be formalized as a set of compatibility constraints; 2) a memory constraint graph can be used as a tool to analyze the compatibility of signals; 3) a new approach to implementing signals (age vectors) is presented, which is based on the maturing process of the signals and the memory constraints graph
we have developed a memory aware HLS tool and a new approach to ageing vectors that can be used to implement signals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions : - How to take into account memory architecture constraints during behavioral synthesis? - What is the best way to implement memory-mapped signals in an HLS context?
the following questions: How to take into account a memory architecture in a HLS tool? How to implement ageing vectors?
the design of a HLS tool that takes into account the memory constraints.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our HLS algorithm provides an interesting alternative to existing tools, especially when the design is memory constrained.
the approach proposed here has been proven to be efficient in practice, with the ability to deal with a wide range of applications, and that the results obtained are very encouraging.
our approach allows the designer to obtain a correct mapping for his design.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a memory aware HLS tool that can handle complex designs and that provides the designer with a set of compatible mappings.
we have developed a memory aware HLS tool and we have proposed a new approach for implementing ageing vectors in a HLS tool.

the memory-aware scheduling and memory-aware implementation techniques have been successfully applied on a set of benchmarks, and the results show that the proposed techniques are able to generate efficient RTL designs with respect to memory utilization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ageing vectors approach allows us to generate code that is more efficient in term of memory usage and memory access time, and that is compatible with any memory architecture.
we are able to generate a memory aware design that is compatible with the memory architecture.
we have shown that it is possible to take into account both memory architecture and memory mapping in behavioral HDL synthesis.
